Feature property scatter plot between two datasets

Source: R/plot_scatter.R
plot_scatter.Rd

Compares two per-feature numeric properties. Features present in both input tables are matched by Feature and plotted using the selected numeric column from each table on the x- and y-axes. When df2 is NULL, two columns from df1 are compared.

Usage

plot_scatter(
  df1,
  df2 = NULL,
  col1,
  col2,
  name1 = NULL,
  name2 = NULL,
  highlight_features = NULL,
  label_top_n = 0,
  label_threshold = NULL,
  show_cor = TRUE,
  cor_method = c("spearman", "pearson", "kendall"),
  colour_threshold = NULL,
  fontsize = 8,
  show_diagonal = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

df1

Data frame with columns Feature and a numeric value column (e.g., logFC, variance proportion).

df2

Optional data frame for the second property. When NULL, df1 is used for both properties.

col1

Name of the numeric column in df1 to plot on the x-axis (e.g., "logFC").

col2

Name of the numeric column in df2 to plot on the y-axis.

name1

Label for dataset 1 (x-axis). Default: "Dataset 1: <col1>".

name2

Label for dataset 2 (y-axis). Default: "Dataset 2: <col2>".

highlight_features

Optional: character vector of feature names to label and mark in black. Features not shared by both datasets are reported and ignored.

label_top_n

Number of top features to label per quadrant. Can be:

  • A single integer: same number of labels for all four quadrants.

  • A vector of 4 integers: labels for quadrants (++, +-, -+, –) respectively. Use c(5, 3, 3, 5) or named c("++"=5, "+-"=3, "-+"=3, "--"=5). Within each quadrant, features are ranked by distance from origin (sqrt(x^2 + y^2)). These features are labelled along with threshold-qualified and highlighted features. Default: 0 (no additional labels).

label_threshold

Minimum absolute value for labelling. A single value applies to both axes, or use a named numeric vector, e.g., c(x = 1, y = 0.5). Both the absolute x and absolute y values must meet their respective thresholds. Qualifying features are labelled along with the top-N and highlighted features. Default: NULL.

show_cor

If TRUE (default), annotate the plot with the correlation coefficient and p-value between the two properties.

cor_method

Correlation method: "spearman" (default), "pearson", or "kendall".

colour_threshold

Minimum absolute value for point colouring. A single value applies to both axes, or use a named numeric vector, e.g., c(x = 1, y = 0.5). Points are coloured only when both absolute x and y values meet their respective thresholds; points below either threshold are shown as grey. Default: NULL (colour all points).

fontsize

Base font size (default: 8).

show_diagonal

If NULL (default), show the dashed y = x line when comparing the same property across two data frames. Set TRUE or FALSE to override this behaviour.

...

Additional arguments passed to ggrepel::geom_text_repel() for controlling label appearance.

Value

A ggplot object of scatter plot.

Examples

# Simulated per-feature numeric properties
df_1 <- data.frame(
    Feature = paste0("Gene", 1:100),
    Property_1 = rnorm(100, 0, 2),
    Property_2 = rnorm(100, 0, 1),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_2 <- data.frame(
    Feature = paste0("Gene", 1:100),
    Property_1 = rnorm(100, 0, 2),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
plot_scatter(df_1, df_2,
    col1 = "Property_1", col2 = "Property_1",
    colour_threshold = 1, label_top_n = 5,
    highlight_features = c("Gene1", "Gene2", "Gene3")
)

# Per-quadrant control: 5 labels in concordant, 2 in discordant
plot_scatter(df_1, df_2,
    col1 = "Property_1", col2 = "Property_1",
    colour_threshold = 1,
    label_top_n = c("++" = 5, "+-" = 2, "-+" = 2, "--" = 5)
)

# Compare two properties from one data frame
plot_scatter(df_1, col1 = "Property_1", col2 = "Property_2",
    colour_threshold = 1, label_top_n = 5)
